props.title: 13 Going on 30
props.initialSlug: A teen's wish turns her 30, but is it what she wanted?

sections.content: **13 Going on 30** (2004) perfectly captures the "body-swap" comedy genre while adding a unique time-travel twist. Jennifer Garner shines as Jenna Rink, a 13-year-old who wakes up in her 30-year-old body, bringing authentic teenage awkwardness to her adult character. The film follows the tradition of age-transformation classics like **Big** (1988) and **Freaky Friday** (2003), but stands apart by exploring millennial nostalgia and female ambition in magazine publishing. The 80s references, including the iconic "Thriller" dance sequence, tap into both genuine period detail and our rose-tinted memories of that era.

sections.content: The film's success sparked a wave of nostalgic coming-of-age stories that examine the transition to adulthood through a magical lens. **Suddenly 30** (2004) - the Australian title for 13 Going on 30 - influenced later works like **17 Again** (2009) and **The Change-Up** (2011). These films share a common thread of characters discovering that their idealized adult lives aren't what they imagined, leading to personal growth and appreciation for authenticity over success.

The chemistry between Jennifer Garner and Mark Ruffalo set a new standard for romantic comedy partnerships. Their relationship echoes elements of **When Harry Met Sally** (1989) in its friends-to-lovers trajectory, while the workplace drama aspects recall **Working Girl** (1988). The film's exploration of female friendship, particularly through the complex relationship between Jenna and Lucy (Judy Greer), adds depth rarely seen in magical transformation comedies. sections.content: The film's portrayal of 80s and early 2000s fashion became instantly iconic. Jenna's colorful wardrobe influenced real-world fashion trends, similar to how **Clueless** (1995) defined 90s teen style. The soundtrack, featuring Michael Jackson, Pat Benatar, and Whitney Houston, created a perfect time capsule that continues to resonate with audiences discovering the film today. The magazine industry setting, while glamorized, captures the cutthroat nature of publishing similar to **The Devil Wears Prada** (2006).
